chunks.arabic_text: أَبِي رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ أَهْلِ السَّمَاءِ هَلْ يَرَوْنَ أَهْلَ الْأَرْضِ

translations.en: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about the inhabitants of the heaven, whether they see the inhabitants of the earth.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ ع لَا يَرَوْنَ إِلَّا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لِأَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ مِنْ نُورٍ كَنُورِ الْكَوَاكِبِ قِيلَ فَهُمْ يَرَوْنَ أَهْلَ الْأَرْضِ قَالَ ع لَا يَرَوْنَ نُورَهُ حَيْثُ مَا تَوَجَّهَ

translations.en: He (peace be upon him) said: They do not see except the believers, because the believer is from light, like the light of the stars. It was said: So do they see the people of the earth? He (peace be upon him) said: No, they do not see their light wherever it turns.

chunks.arabic_text: ثُمَّ قَالَ ع لِكُلِّ مُُوْمِنٍ خَمْسُ سَاعَاتٍ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَشْفَعُ فِيهَا

translations.en: Then he (peace be upon him) added: For every believer there are five hours on the Day of Resurrection during which he will intercede.

en.summary: In this narration from *Sifat al-Shia*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical nature of believers as beings of light (*nur*), explaining that their spiritual radiance allows them to be perceived in the heavens while their light remains distinct from the general populace on earth. This concept underscores the unique ontological status of the faithful in Shia cosmology, linking their earthly conduct to their eschatological role, specifically highlighting the privilege of intercession (*shafa'ah*) granted to each believer for five hours on the Day of Judgment.
en.seo_question: Can the inhabitants of heaven see people on earth, and what is the significance of the believer's light?
